name: NUGGET BACK ROOM
note: EXTRACTED by tools/extract-examine.mjs from the documents its sources name -- errata 67's merge, in doc 05's, the batch's, then the repeats' order, less errata 68 H's drops. Do not edit: change the documents and re-run.

subjects.name: THE LONG TABLE
LOOK_AT: One table, two chairs facing, and a great deal of floor for standing around it. The architecture of an argument.
A table, three chairs, and a great deal of authority for a room behind a saloon.
The top is scored with knife marks in tallies of five, older than the scoreboard. Somebody kept count before there was a slate to keep it on.
LISTEN_TO: The wood is still. Between duels it keeps its own counsel.
Nothing. It is waiting to be sat at, which is most of what furniture does here.
A knuckle rapping it, somewhere in memory. The table remembers every point of order.

subjects.name: THE JUDGES' PENCIL
LOOK_AT: The pencil the judges score with, chained to the table like something precious. It is sharpened at both ends, which nobody will explain.
It has been sharpened so often there is very little pencil left between the two points. Justice, worn to a stub.
There are tooth marks on it, at both ends. The judges deliberate in the usual way.
LISTEN_TO: Nothing. It has written every verdict in town and holds no opinion.
Nothing.
The chain clinking against the table leg when the door opens.

overrides.PICK_UP: Chained, and the chain is newer than the pencil. There is a story and nobody will tell it to a newcomer.

subjects.name: THE SCOREBOARD
LOOK_AT: A slate of past Assays. The same three names win and the same eleven lose, and all fourteen keep playing.
Duels won, by name, in chalk, going back years. Deke Vessel has forty-one. Nickel Pratt has nine, which surprises me. Colonel Fanshawe has none — because Colonel Fanshawe has never entered.
The chalk on the oldest names has been gone over again and again, so it will not fade. Losing is kept up as carefully as winning.
LISTEN_TO: Chalk dust, settling. The sound of standings.
Nothing.
Nothing, then a crumb of chalk dropping from the ledge. History, settling.

overrides.USE: Amending the slate is how the last man lost his chalk privileges, and the story is told as a tragedy.

subjects.name: THE LAMP OVER THE TABLE
LOOK_AT: Hung low, so the light lands on the liars and leaves the judges dark. Somebody thought about this.
The chain it hangs from has been shortened twice, a link at a time. The liars have been getting closer to the light.
Its shade is painted green inside, which makes everyone under it look slightly unwell and entirely sincere.
LISTEN_TO: The flame leans when the door opens. It attends every duel.
The flame, leaning toward the door and settling back.
A low hiss. The lamp is the only one here that never exaggerates.

subjects.name: THE CHAIRS
LOOK_AT: Two chairs, worn in different places. The challenger's is worn at the edge of the seat; the champion's, at the back.
The challenger's chair has a short leg. Nobody has fixed it, because nobody thinks the challenger should be comfortable.
The champion's chair has a cushion. It was won, I am told, in a duel about the cushion.
LISTEN_TO: A creak waiting to happen.
The short leg, rocking once as I touch it.
Nothing. Two chairs, facing, saying nothing to each other.

overrides.TALK_TO: 'One day,' I told the champion's chair. It creaked. Not unkindly.

subjects.name: THE DOOR TO THE BAR
LOOK_AT: The noise of the Nugget comes through it in outline. Bets travel the other way.
There is a slot at eye height, with a shutter, so the bar can be told the result without the bar being let in.
The paint is worn around the handle by men coming in confident and going out otherwise.
LISTEN_TO: Money, changing its mind.
The bar. Muffled. Somebody out there has told the same story four times and it has grown twice.
A cheer, through the boards, for something that has nothing to do with in here.

subjects.name: THE SPIT LINE
LOOK_AT: A line scored in the floorboards. You stand behind it to boast. The floor in front of it is stained with the history of emphasis.
Some men stand a long way behind it. Some stand on it. Nobody stands in front of it, twice.
Someone has gone over it with a hot iron to keep it from wearing away. The line is the most maintained thing in the Nugget.
LISTEN_TO: Nothing. The line has heard it all twice.
Nothing. It is a line, and it is enough.
Nothing. The boasts it has heard have all gone into the floor.

overrides.PUSH: You cannot move the line. Men have tried. The line is load-bearing, socially.

subjects.name: THE WINDOW, PAINTED OVER
LOOK_AT: Painted over from the inside. What happens in the Assay is public and the window is not. I do not fully follow the reasoning either.
Someone has scratched a small hole in the paint at the corner, at eye height, the size of an eye.
The paint is the same green as the lamp shade. Somebody had a theory about green.
LISTEN_TO: Wind on glass, dulled by paint. The outside, filed away.
The wind, filed under 'outside', and a cart going by in the margin.
Nothing. The window is keeping the room's confidence.

subjects.name: THE SECOND RULEBOOK
LOOK_AT: A longer copy of the rules, in a binder, with amendments. There are fourteen amendments. Eleven of them concern seating.
Amendment Nine: no man may boast of his own mother. Amendment Ten: or anybody else's.
The binder's spine is held together with string, and the string has an amendment of its own.
LISTEN_TO: Nothing.
A page turning back on its own, to the seating rules.
Nothing. Fourteen amendments, at rest.

subjects.name: THE RING OF CHAIRS
LOOK_AT: Chairs, in a ring, close in. Whatever happens in here happens with everyone's knees nearly touching.
The chairs nearest the table are worn at the front edge. Everybody leans in.
There are more chairs than there are men in town who come to duels. Somebody is optimistic about attendance.
LISTEN_TO: Nothing yet.
One chair creaking as the floor shifts. An audience of one, getting comfortable.
Nothing. The ring is waiting for the next fool, and I am standing in the middle of it.

subjects.name: THE CHALK
LOOK_AT: A stub of chalk on the scoreboard's ledge, worn to the shape of a thumb.
It is kept in a little tin with a lid. Chalk has been stolen here before, I am told, by a man who meant to change history.
Only the judges may touch it. It is the most powerful object in the territory and it is the size of a bean.
LISTEN_TO: Nothing. Chalk at rest is silent.
The tin lid, ticking as the room warms.
Nothing. It speaks once a duel, on slate, and then it is done.

DEKE VESSEL.PICK_UP (in a duel): Not across the line. There are amendments.

THE JUDGES.TALK_TO (in a duel): They are deliberating. I can hear them chewing the pencil.
THE JUDGES.USE: Nobody uses the judges. That is the one thing everyone here agrees on.
